title: Databricks Workspace Request
description: Request submitted to the Databricks workspace factory for provisioning a workspace.

databricks_account_id.description: Override the AWS account's default Databricks account (platform/inventory/aws.yaml's 'aws.accounts.<name>.databricks_account_id'). Optional - most workspaces don't need this; it exists for the rare case a workspace must land in a different Databricks account than its AWS account's default.

connectivity.description: How isolated-strategy classic compute reaches the Databricks control plane. 'privatelink' requires an Enterprise-tier Databricks account (rejected otherwise); 'nat' always builds a NAT Gateway; 'auto' (default if omitted) picks PrivateLink when the target Databricks account supports it, NAT otherwise. Moot for 'custom' strategy workspaces reusing an existing VPC's own connectivity. Azure (CLAUDE.md §8 milestone 46): 'privatelink' turns on classic (back-end) Private Link; 'auto'/omitted turns it on in stage/live and leaves it off in dev; 'nat' is rejected.

vpc_cidr.description: CIDR block for a new, dedicated VPC. Required for 'isolated' strategy (or any workspace whose VPC ownership otherwise resolves to 'terraform') - this is the client's own address-space choice, not an operator- or platform-invented value. Checked for pool containment/collisions by resolver/check_cidr_allocations.py. Ignored for 'custom' strategy workspaces reusing an existing VPC.

existing_vpc_id.description: ID of an existing VPC the client is handing over for 'custom' strategy. Optional - when omitted, the AWS account's known 'primary' network (platform/inventory/aws.yaml) is used by default, same as today. Azure: the full resource id of the client's VNet (/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/<name>) - required for Azure 'custom', no inventory default.

existing_vpc_cidr.description: CIDR block of the VPC named by existing_vpc_id, needed only when that VPC is not already known in platform/inventory/aws.yaml - lets subnet auto-allocation know the address space to carve from. Ignored if the VPC is already known in inventory. Azure: one of the VNet's address-space ranges, required for Azure 'custom' unless existing_subnet_ids is given (there is no Azure inventory to look it up from).

existing_security_group_id.description: ID of an existing security group the client is handing over, instead of one Terraform creates. Optional - when present, security group ownership automatically resolves to 'existing' (no separate ownership override needed).

existing_route_table_ids.description: IDs of existing route tables the client's existing VPC (existing_vpc_id) already has, for Terraform to attach new subnets to instead of creating fresh route tables. Optional - when present, routing (and, by default, endpoints) ownership automatically resolves to 'existing'. Omit when the VPC has no usable route tables yet (e.g. a bare VPC) - routing then correctly resolves to 'terraform'.

existing_private_dns_zone_ids.description: Azure only, with Private Link: full resource ids of existing hub private DNS zones for privatelink.azuredatabricks.net, privatelink.dfs.core.windows.net and privatelink.blob.core.windows.net (all three), used instead of per-workspace zones. Needed when several Private Link workspaces share a client VNet. Records are written into these zones, so the deployer needs rights on them.

existing_subnet_ids.description: IDs of existing subnets inside existing_vpc_id to use for the workspace, instead of having Terraform create new ones. Optional - omit for Terraform to auto-allocate and create new subnets (today's default). Known limitation: because these subnets' CIDRs are never looked up, they're invisible to resolver/check_cidr_allocations.py's collision checker - avoid also using auto-allocation for a sibling workspace in the same VPC. Azure: exactly two, [public, private] in that order, each already delegated to Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces with an NSG associated.

existing_workspace_storage_key_arn.description: ARN of an existing customer-managed KMS key to use for workspace storage (DBFS/root-bucket/EBS), instead of a dedicated one the platform creates. Only meaningful when encryption.workspace resolves to 'customer_managed' (profile/policy-derived, not requester-controlled). Optional.

existing_workspace_storage_key_alias.description: Alias name of the existing workspace storage key named above, if any.

existing_managed_services_key_arn.description: ARN of an existing customer-managed KMS key to use for Databricks control-plane managed services data, instead of a dedicated one the platform creates. Optional.

existing_managed_services_key_alias.description: Alias name of the existing managed services key named above, if any.

existing_workspace_storage_key_id.description: Azure only: full ARM resource id of an existing Key Vault key (/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>/keys/<key>) for managed disks + DBFS root, instead of one the platform creates. The vault must be RBAC-mode with purge protection, in the workspace's region and tenant, and the deploying identity must be able to assign roles on it. Only meaningful when encryption.workspace resolves to 'customer_managed'.

existing_managed_services_key_id.description: Azure only: full ARM resource id of an existing Key Vault key for managed services (notebooks, secrets, queries). Same vault requirements as existing_workspace_storage_key_id.

existing_application_data_key_id.description: Azure only: full ARM resource id of an existing Key Vault key for the Unity Catalog storage account. Same vault requirements as existing_workspace_storage_key_id. Only meaningful when encryption.application_data resolves to 'customer_managed'.

catalog_admin_principal.description: A Databricks user name, group name, or service principal application ID to grant ALL_PRIVILEGES on this workspace's Unity Catalog catalog. Optional - omit to leave the catalog ungranted (owner defaults to whoever runs terraform apply).

compliance_standards.description: Regulatory compliance standards this workspace must satisfy (e.g. 'HIPAA', 'PCI_DSS', 'FEDRAMP_MODERATE', 'FEDRAMP_HIGH', 'IRAP' - see the Databricks provider's ComplianceStandard enum for valid values, not re-validated here). Optional - omitting this (the default) leaves Compliance Security Profile, Enhanced Security Monitoring, and Automatic Cluster Update all off, since enabling them incurs the Enhanced Security and Compliance billing add-on. Only the requester knows what regulatory context a workspace actually needs.

existing_metastore_id.description: Override the Unity Catalog metastore this workspace is assigned to, instead of the Databricks account/region's known default (platform/inventory/aws.yaml). Optional - most workspaces don't need this.
